stories.Headline: US to tell partners to pick side in AI race
stories.Summary:
The United States is preparing to inform dozens of countries that they must choose between American and Chinese artificial intelligence initiatives, threatening to exclude nations from a US-led AI coalition if they also participate in Beijing's competing framework. This ultimatum comes as Washington continues its fierce technology competition with China. The US launched the Pax Silica initiative last year to secure supply chains for AI models, semiconductors, and critical minerals, and currently has about two dozen members including Japan, Australia, and South Korea, as well as Kazakhstan.

A draft State Department letter addresses 35 signatories of a US AI Opportunity Statement signed in June. The move follows China's launch of a rival World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization in July, which promotes Chinese open-weight technology. Kazakhstan has joined both initiatives, raising concerns in Washington. The letter will reportedly pressure countries to commit exclusively to either the American or Chinese framework in the escalating technological rivalry between the two powers.

stories.Headline: India's Manufacturing Future Will Be Built by Engineers Who Understand How the World's Best Products Are Made
stories.Summary:
Caresoft Global and DRIIV, a research organization under India's Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, have partnered to improve engineering talent in India. The collaboration aims to expose engineering students to global manufacturing practices and real-world product development, addressing a critical gap in India's workforce as the country shifts toward higher-value manufacturing in electric vehicles and electronics-intensive products. Adroit Technologies will serve as the implementation partner.

The initiative will establish Centers of Excellence across India, offering focused training programs in emerging technology areas including electric vehicles, software-defined vehicles, battery systems, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence. The partnership will leverage Caresoft Global's Iceberg platform, which analyzes how leading manufacturers make decisions on design, performance, and cost. The goal is to bridge the divide between India's strong theoretical engineering education and practical knowledge of how world-class products are actually engineered and manufactured.

stories.Headline: NIELIT Launches CYBER KUSHTI 2026: National Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon scores judgment rather than detection speed
stories.Summary:
NIELIT, the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology, launched CYBER KUSHTI 2026 on August 15th as a national cybersecurity and artificial intelligence hackathon. The competition differs from traditional cybersecurity contests by focusing on human judgment rather than speed of detection. Free registration opened on August 15th and closes September 10th, with teams of three students and independent researchers eligible to participate. Each team receives an identical package containing deliberately flawed security assessments with false findings, duplicates, and omissions to evaluate and prioritize.

The hackathon unfolds in three rounds, starting with an online round on September 15th selecting 50 teams, followed by another online round on September 24th narrowing to 10 finalists. The final round occurs in person on October 9th in New Delhi at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre. Judges from government, industry, and academia will evaluate participants' ability to identify genuine issues and correctly reject false findings. The winning team receives the title "Cyber Kesari 2026," while runners-up receive "Rustam" and "Pahalwan" titles.

stories.Headline: 'Nation First-Rashtra Pratham' should remain the guiding principle: VP Radhakrishnan at SRMIST convocation
stories.Summary:
Vice President CP Radhakrishnan addressed the 22nd convocation at SRM Institute of Science and Technology in Chennai, urging graduating students to adopt "Nation First - Rashtra Pratham" as their guiding principle. He emphasized that graduates should use their knowledge, skills and innovation for nation-building and preparing themselves to shape the future. Radhakrishnan praised the institution's focus on emerging fields including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductor research and sustainable development, noting that research achieves its highest purpose when it serves society and produces practical benefits for people.

The Vice President highlighted India's educational expansion since 2014, with the establishment of numerous universities and institutes across the country. He noted that female enrollment in higher education increased by 42.2 percent from 2014-15 to 2023-24, rising from 1.57 crore to 2.24 crore students. Radhakrishnan also urged graduates to avoid drugs and substance abuse, referencing a recent tragic incident in Tamil Nadu. He encouraged students to uphold constitutional values, respect diversity and place national interest above personal gain, while embodying the Indian values of knowledge, duty, compassion and service.

stories.Headline: Over 4,000 abandoned mine pits in Plateau – Alake
stories.Summary:
The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, reported that over 4,000 abandoned mine pits are scattered across Plateau State. These pits, largely created by former mining companies, present serious environmental and safety hazards. The announcement came after seven people died in a collapsed mine pit in Kassa, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area. Alake emphasized that the tragedy was preventable and warned unauthorized artisanal miners against entering abandoned pits without proper licenses and permits.

The federal government has already rehabilitated 59 of these abandoned pits and plans to rehabilitate more. Alake stated that the ministry is using Geographic Information System satellite mapping and artificial intelligence technology to identify and assess the remaining pits, with Plateau serving as the initial pilot location. The minister encouraged private investors to partner with the government to convert these abandoned sites into productive ventures such as energy, tourism, and fisheries projects. He also called on miners to organize into cooperatives and obtain necessary legal approvals to operate properly.

stories.Headline: New EU laws make AI content labels compulsory – but might just make it harder to spot deepfakes - 17-Aug-2026
stories.Summary:
The European Union has begun enforcing new laws requiring technology companies to label AI-generated content such as photos, videos, and audio that are designed to appear authentic. These rules took effect on August 2 and apply to companies worldwide if their content reaches EU users. Non-compliant companies face fines up to 15 million euros or 3 percent of annual worldwide revenue. The regulations also require invisible, machine-readable watermarks on AI-generated content, though disclosure requirements do not apply to individuals creating content personally.

However, researchers warn that labeling alone may not effectively combat deepfakes and could create unintended problems. People may assume unlabeled content is real, potentially making them more vulnerable to deceptive material that deliberately lacks disclosure labels. Critical evaluation of online content requires more than just identifying labels. Experts emphasize that citizens need improved AI literacy, including awareness of suspicious details and source credibility, because AI technology continues to become more sophisticated and harder to detect through visual cues alone.

stories.Headline: Amazon vs. Microsoft: Which Cloud Computing Behemoth Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Buy Today?
stories.Summary:
# Summary

Amazon and Microsoft are major players in artificial intelligence and cloud computing, with both companies integrating AI into their products while using external AI models rather than developing their own. Both have diversified business operations that provide stability regardless of economic conditions, with Microsoft operating in business software, gaming, and cloud services, while Amazon dominates online commerce and cloud infrastructure through AWS. The article evaluates both companies across several categories including business breadth, growth rates, and valuation metrics.

Amazon emerges as the stronger investment choice based on its superior growth trajectory and valuation. Amazon's AWS cloud division recently accelerated to 37 percent growth after years of slower expansion, positioning it to maintain momentum as AI spending continues rising. Additionally, Amazon demonstrates stronger operating profit growth and appears cheaper on forward earnings projections. While Microsoft remains a solid investment with considerable upside potential, the article concludes that Amazon currently offers more growth opportunity in the near term.

stories.Headline: Gujarat Police plans single network for 80,000 CCTV cameras, through AI-enabled hackathon
stories.Summary:
Gujarat Police is organizing a major hackathon called the Gujarat Police Innovation Challenge 2026 to integrate over 80,000 surveillance cameras statewide into a single network. The initiative brings together students, startups, technology companies, developers, and researchers to create artificial intelligence tools that can help police forces work more effectively. The challenge aims to solve the problem of CCTV cameras from different vendors operating separately and unable to share information seamlessly.

Participants will develop systems capable of identifying suspicious people and vehicles, tracking activities in real time, and recognizing license plates across multiple cameras. The competition runs in two stages, with the six best teams advancing to a final round demonstrating their solutions using real-world policing scenarios. The hackathon, set to begin in September under the leadership of the Director General of Police, offers total cash prizes of 37 lakh rupees and receives support from technology partners and universities.

stories.Headline: Why CISOs Must Become Chief Trust Officers for AI
stories.Summary:
Chief Information Security Officers must expand their role to become trust leaders for artificial intelligence systems within their organizations. According to Forrester analyst Jess Burn, boards and executives are pushing for faster AI adoption, which strains security teams' ability to maintain proper controls. This tension creates an opportunity for CISOs to position themselves as trust and assurance leaders rather than simply blocking progress. Burn noted that CISOs faced similar challenges during the cloud computing era, when they were initially sidelined and later blamed for security failures like exposed data buckets.

External stakeholders including regulators, cyber insurers, customers, and business partners now require proof that AI systems will not endanger data or business operations. This shift allows CISOs to take the lead on establishing trust in AI before security incidents occur and force reactive measures. The article suggests that some level of concern about AI risks is necessary to help organizations understand the importance of proper security and governance frameworks before problems emerge.

stories.Headline: Palantir Technologies Inc. $PLTR Shares Sold by Oppenheimer Asset Management Inc.
stories.Summary:
Oppenheimer Asset Management Inc. reduced its stake in Palantir Technologies by 14.1% during the second quarter, selling 14,080 shares and retaining 85,647 shares worth approximately 10 million dollars, according to its most recent SEC filing. Several other institutional investors and hedge funds have also adjusted their positions in the company, with some establishing new stakes while others increased their holdings during recent quarters. Institutional investors and hedge funds collectively own about 45.65% of Palantir's outstanding stock.

Palantir Technologies reported strong second quarter earnings with revenue of 1.94 billion dollars, up 92.8% year-over-year, and earnings per share of 0.41 dollars, beating analyst expectations. The company's stock was trading at 174.04 dollars with a market capitalization of 418.23 billion dollars. Most analysts maintain a moderate buy rating with a consensus target price of 192.19 dollars, though some express concerns about the company's high valuation at more than 400 billion dollars and its elevated earnings multiple.
